newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Work on Russian tax code seen taking 18 months.
newsitem.headline: Work on Russian tax code seen taking 18 months.

text.p: The new Russian tax code will need at least 18 months of work in parliament, a member of the State Duma lower house said on Monday.
"Judging by experience, it is clear that a minimum of 1-1/2 years' work (is needed)," Alexander Pochinok, deputy head of the Duma's budget sub-committee, told a news conference.

The government has long delayed reform of Russia's convoluted and often arbitrary tax system but work on the legislation has acquired a new urgency after the visit of the International Monetary Fund chief Michel Camdessus last week.

Camdessus said the IMF will release the next tranche of its $10 billion three-year loan to Russia only when the government has submitted the full draft of the new code to the Duma, which has so far received only the first of four parts.
But approving the code, seen as a precondition for passing realistic budgets, could take much longer, in part due to strong Duma opposition to abolishing tax breaks.
